title: Stripe retries vanish after attempt two

scenes.label: before lunch · 12:40
scenes.title: Stripe retries vanish after attempt two

lines.say: You were chasing the Stripe webhook retries that vanish after the second attempt.
Attempt one fails. Attempt two fails. And then, nothing. There's no third attempt in the logs at all.
lines.show: attempt 1 fails · attempt 2 fails · then nothing

lines.say: First you suspected the backoff math in retry policy. But you checked it. Four seconds, sixteen, sixty-four. It's fine.
What's still open is where the retry lives between attempts.
lines.show: where the retry lives between attempts

lines.say: Here's what you think is going on. An attempt fails,
the worker acks the job first,
and only then schedules the retry, and only in memory.
Then the worker restarts, which it does, because of the memory limit.
And the pending retry dies with it. That's why there's never a third attempt.
lines.note: the retry dies with the worker

lines.say: The idea you hadn't finished: schedule the retry in the database, in the same transaction that marks the attempt failed.
lines.show: schedule the retry in the database
lines.sub: same transaction that marks the attempt failed

lines.say: What you don't know yet is whether the queue library can do delayed jobs on the Postgres adapter.
lines.show: delayed jobs on the Postgres adapter?

lines.say: One trap. Don't trust the dashboard count.
It dedupes by event ID, so it would hide a third attempt even if one happened.
lines.sub: a third attempt would be hidden

scenes.label: where to look

lines.say: When you sit back down, open handle webhook, around line forty.
The question is whether ack gets called before schedule retry.
So, first move. Add a log line right there, and replay event one Q eight with the replay script.
lines.show: Log ack vs. scheduleRetry, replay evt_1Q8

lines.say: If no retry shows up after a restart, your theory holds.
lines.show: no retry after a restart → theory holds
